I've been farming this same land in Quzhou for fifty years. I know these fields. The wheat goes in come October, maize follows after the wheat harvest in June — same ground, same rotation I've done my whole life. My children help during the busy seasons since my body isn't what it was, but I still make the decisions.

For wheat, I'll plant about 16 mu — the whole plot. I'll buy improved seed from the township supply station, the semi-dwarf variety they've been selling around here for years. Good tillering, doesn't lodge easily. I'll run the rotary tiller after we pull the maize stalks in October, then apply base fertilizer before seeding. I put down compound fertilizer at planting and then urea at jointing — my father did it this way, I do it this way. With the well, I'll water before winter sets in, again at jointing, and once more at heading. Three times is what wheat needs here. I'll spray for aphids and do one herbicide pass in spring. I expect around 480 jin per mu if the weather holds.

For maize, same 16 mu starting June. I'll use hybrid seed — everyone does now, the yield difference is real and I've seen it myself. After we cut wheat I'll direct-seed into the stubble, no need to plow twice in one summer, saves my son a day's work. I apply urea in two shots — some at planting, the rest when it's knee-high. Summer rains usually carry us through but I'll run the well once if July turns dry. One pesticide pass for corn borer is enough. I expect around 550 jin per mu.
